messages:
Anya: Quick FYI 10k smoke for the new reranker (rbk-3b-v2) turned up inconsistent regressions across backends. posting protocol and early notes here.
Luis: What inconsistencies? numbers?
Anya: aggregated: hosted int8 NDCG@10 -0.7% vs hosted fp16; dedicated int8 -0.15%. MRR follows similar pattern.
Maya: Huh. Did you lock tokenizer & candidate ordering? we saw order drift cause large-looking deltas before.
Anya: Yes locked both. Also ran 3 seeds per config. command used:
```bash
eval-run --model rbk-3b-v2 --backends hosted,dedicated --qtypes int8,fp16 \
  --cohort strat20k --seeds 42,84,128 --keep-order --normalize-candidates
```
Luis: Could be kernel selection differences or microbatching/seed in batching. Any kernel flags for hosted?
Anya: Hosted auto picks kernel A for int8; dedicated used kernel B. I couldn't pin hosted without infra assist.
Maya: What about per-query margin distribution? are regressions concentrated in low-margin ties?
Anya: Yes ~60% of swaps are margin <0.03. But there are ~1.1% of queries with >0.1 score swing.
infra-bot: upload: s3://redwood-evals/rbk3b/v2/3102001234/ (hosted/dedicated folders)
Luis: Can you post a few minimal examples where order flips? helps triage numeric vs data issues.
Anya: sample ids: 3344, 7780, 9901. Example snippet:
"query: how to seed shuffling in tf.data"
fp16 top: doc about tf.data.shuffle(seed=...) score 0.81
int8 top: doc about manual seed in python -> score 0.83
Maya: borderline indeed. that could be tiny logit nudges. Is softmax temperature different between backends?
Anya: Same serving config. suspect kernel numerics + prefix kvcache accumulation differences.
Luis: Let's run three quick diagnostics: 1) force hosted to use kernel B (match dedicated). 2) disable prefix cache on all backends. 3) rerun on a larger borderline set (margin <0.05) with 100k queries.
Anya: Agreed. I'll file infra request for kernel pin. Also will create run with cache disabled.
infra-bot: task created INFRA-892 (kernel pin request), EVAL-334 (cache-disabled run).
Maya: If pinning fixes it we might need to change hosted selection policy or add a numeric-stability test to CI.
Luis: Also check tokenizer postprocessing: we canonicalize whitespace and strip HTML, but ensure same unicode normal form across pipelines. tiny norm differences can shift tokenization and subsequent logit alignment.
Anya: Good catch. I'll add unicode normalization check and include serialized token ids in the run artifacts.
Maya: Ops note: if we see top1 swap >2% we should pause rollout. I'll write a short runbook.
Anya: Will follow up with results in-thread once experiments finish. thanks. :mag:
